text:
Who does not weep for what is past?

        Who does not weep for what is past,

seeing how the present goes?

Who is

        the one who does not feel

what fortune has taken away?

I

        once saw myself well loved,

my desire on a high summit;

to contemplate the

        past-

memory wounds me.

And

        since everything is absent from me,

I do not know which remedy to choose;

good and evil alike

        anger me,

poor wretch who feels it!

        There was a time, and proud hours,

which my life enjoyed,

where sorrowfully

        were sown

the seeds of my gray hairs.

And

        since, if he holds it good,

I can well speak this way.

translation.title: Song
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps this expanded duplicate-body variant's opening refrain and broken manuscript-like spacing.
